Let \(x=x_u\). The problem is equivalent to maximizing
\[
\int_0^1 x(t)^3\,dt
\]
over absolutely continuous \(x\) such that
\[
x(0)=x(1)=0,\qquad |x'(t)|\le 1\text{ a.e.},\qquad \int_0^1x(t)\,dt=0.
\]

The maximum is
\[
\boxed{\frac1{1458}}.
\]

The optimal controls, up to equality a.e., are exactly the following two time-reversed controls:
\[
u(t)=
\begin{cases}
-1,&0<t<\frac19,\\
0,&\frac19<t<\frac49,\\
1,&\frac49<t<\frac79,\\
-1,&\frac79<t<1,
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
u(t)=
\begin{cases}
1,&0<t<\frac29,\\
-1,&\frac29<t<\frac59,\\
0,&\frac59<t<\frac89,\\
1,&\frac89<t<1.
\end{cases}
\]

For the first one,
\[
x(t)=
\begin{cases}
-t,&0\le t\le \frac19,\\
-\frac19,&\frac19\le t\le \frac49,\\
t-\frac59,&\frac49\le t\le \frac79,\\
1-t,&\frac79\le t\le 1.
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
\int_0^1 x(t)\,dt
=-\frac1{81}-\frac1{27}+\frac4{81}=0,
\]
and
\[
\int_0^1 x(t)^3\,dt
=\frac{(2/9)^4}{2}-\left(\frac{(1/9)^4}{2}+\frac13\left(\frac19\right)^3\right)
=\frac1{1458}.
\]

Here is the sharpness argument. By the usual one-dimensional rearrangement for Lipschitz paths, an optimizer may be taken, up to time reversal, in the form
\[
0\to -b\quad\text{slope }-1,\qquad
\text{flat at }-b,\qquad
-b\to h\quad\text{slope }1,\qquad
\text{flat at }h,\qquad
h\to0\quad\text{slope }-1,
\]
with \(h\ge b\ge0\). This rearrangement preserves the zero-mean condition and cannot decrease \(\int x^3\): positive mass is moved as high as the slope bound permits, while negative mass is spread as evenly as the slope bound permits. Equality forces this single-valley/single-peak shape.

Let the flat times at \(-b\) and \(h\) be \(\alpha,\beta\). The zero-mean condition says
\[
b^2+\alpha b=h^2+\beta h=:A.
\]
The total-time condition is
\[
2b+2h+\alpha+\beta=1,
\]
equivalently
\[
A\left(\frac1b+\frac1h\right)+b+h=1.
\]
The objective equals
\[
J=\frac{h^4-b^4}{2}+\beta h^3-\alpha b^3
=(h^2-b^2)\left(A-\frac{h^2+b^2}{2}\right).
\]

Write \(h=rb\), \(r\ge1\), and \(s=b+h\). Then
\[
A=\frac{bh(1-b-h)}{b+h}
=\frac{rs(1-s)}{(1+r)^2}.
\]
The constraint \(\beta\ge0\) gives \(s\le \frac1{1+r}\). Substitution gives
\[
J=\frac{s^3(r^2-1)}{(1+r)^4}
\left(r(1-s)-\frac{s(r^2+1)}2\right).
\]
For fixed \(r\), this is maximized at
\[
s=\frac{3r}{2(1+r)^2}
\]
when \(1\le r\le2\), and at \(s=\frac1{1+r}\) when \(r\ge2\). In the first case,
\[
J\le \frac{27r^4(r^2-1)}{32(1+r)^{10}},
\]
whose maximum on \([1,2]\) occurs at \(r=2\). In the second case,
\[
J\le \frac{(r-1)^2}{2(r+1)^6},
\]
whose maximum on \([2,\infty)\) also occurs at \(r=2\). Thus \(r=2\), \(s=\frac13\), so
\[
b=\frac19,\qquad h=\frac29,\qquad \alpha=\frac13,\qquad \beta=0.
\]
This gives exactly the two controls listed above, related by time reversal. Hence the maximum is
\[
\boxed{\frac1{1458}}.
\]
